LLM_description:
Situation:
Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Delta are sustaining forward forces operating along contested ground in a mixed urban–rural battlespace. Infantry Battalion Hawk, Armored Company Iron, Recon Squadron Phoenix, and Artillery Battery Echo are drawing critical materiel under persistent harassment from indirect fire, roadside threats, and intermittent interdiction. Ground corridors vary in security posture and transit time; valley approaches are exposed to observation and ambush, while ridge lines are constrained by terrain and weather. Escort teams, route clearance assets, and overwatch elements are required to open and secure movement corridors before any convoy is dispatched.

Mission:
Resupply the forward units from available stocks while minimizing total operational cost, to include transport costs, shortage penalties for unmet demand, per-vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs associated with activating any movement corridor.

Execution/Concept:
- Depot throughput is constrained by available stocks and daily release rates. Outbound allocations from each depot must not exceed on-hand supply for the period.
- Each unit has daily demand that must be covered by deliveries; controlled shortfalls are permitted and tracked as deferred supply, incurring shortage penalties that reflect operational impact.
- Vehicle assignment is limited by fleet availability and per-vehicle capacity. Delivered volume on any depot–unit movement must respect vehicle capacity by supply volume.
- Movement corridors require activation prior to use. Activating a route at any time incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing security overhead (escort teams, route clearance, ISR tasking), independent of the number of vehicles subsequently dispatched on that route.
- Vehicles can only be assigned to routes that have been activated. Total vehicles employed across all depot–unit movements remain within fleet limits.
- Cost-informed routing will prioritize secure, reliable corridors; when risk is acceptable, shipments may be consolidated to reduce the number of activated routes and the associated fixed security overhead. If required, demand may be partially deferred to later periods, balancing shortage penalties against transport, vehicle, and risk costs.
- The plan will sequence convoys to maximize payload utilization, reduce exposure windows, and maintain flexibility to reallocate between depots based on evolving threat, weather, and route status.

LLM_description_template:
Situation:
- Two rear-area hubs, Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Delta, must sustain four forward units operating on dispersed axes over a four-day window. The units are engaged and mobility-limited; their daily requirements for a single critical supply class are time-sensitive.
- Ground lines of communication from each depot to each unit are open but contested. Valley corridors are vulnerable to ambush and IEDs; ridge routes are weather-sensitive; urban approaches require dismounted clearance. Each route has distinct transport costs and a fixed security overhead to activate.
- Depot stocks are constrained by inbound convoys and handling capacity. Fleet availability is limited to a common pool of tactical cargo vehicles. Escorts, route clearance, and QRF coverage are finite and must be prioritized.

Mission:
Deliver the required quantities of the critical supply from available depots to all four supported units across the planning period while minimizing total operational cost, to include:
- Variable transport costs for moving supply along each depot-to-unit route,
- Shortage penalties for any unmet demand,
- Per-vehicle deployment costs,
- Fixed route security risk costs incurred whenever a route is activated on a given day.

Execution/Concept:
- Concept of Support: Allocate daily flows from either depot to each unit along pre-designated MSRs. For any day and route where at least one vehicle is dispatched, the route is considered active and triggers a fixed Risk Cost that covers escorts, route clearance, ISR, and QRF posture—this overhead is incurred regardless of the number of vehicles on that route. To reduce overhead, avoid activating multiple routes where a single secure route suffices.
- Constraints:
  - Depot Capacity: Outbound shipments on any day cannot exceed available stocks at the originating depot.
  - Demand Fulfillment: Each unit’s daily requirement must be met; controlled shortfalls are allowed only at a penalty reflecting operational risk.
  - Vehicle Capacity: Load assignments must respect vehicle cargo capacity by volume for the single supply class.
  - Route Activation: Vehicles may only move on routes formally activated for that day; activation is binary and drives the fixed Risk Cost.
  - Fleet Size: Total vehicles dispatched across all routes on any day cannot exceed the fleet available.
- Cost Discipline: The optimization will select depot-to-unit flows and convoy assignments by day to minimize the sum of transport costs, shortage penalties, per-vehicle costs, and fixed route Risk Costs. Preference is given to concentrating shipments on fewer, safer routes when feasible, using the closer depot when stocks permit, and smoothing deliveries to reduce peak-day fleet demand and repeated activations.
- Risk Mitigation: When high-risk corridors must be opened, consolidate loads to limit the number of activations. Employ alternate routes during adverse weather and reserve vehicles for priority units when depot stocks are constrained.
